## 6. An exact all-input purity boundary

Here is the complete structural theorem obtained during the analytic investigation.

For every finite \(n\) and every genuinely mixed \(n\)-mode state \(\rho\), define
\[
P_B=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[\mathcal N_x^{\otimes n}(\rho)^2\right],
\qquad
P_E=\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[((\mathcal N_x^c)^{\otimes n}(\rho))^2\right].
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{sign}(P_E-P_B)
=
\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\frac12-x\right).
}
\]

This includes correlated non-Gaussian inputs. No energy assumption is needed for this bounded-operator statement. Pure inputs have equal purities at every \(x\); at \(x=1/2\), equality holds for every input.

### Proof mechanism

Let \(F\) exchange two copies of the entire \(n\)-mode input, and put
\[
M=(\mathcal N_x^{*\otimes n}\otimes\mathcal N_x^{*\otimes n})(F).
\]
The Stinespring swap identities give
\[
P_B=\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho\otimes\rho)M],
\qquad
P_E=\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho\otimes\rho)MF].
\]

Pairwise balanced beamsplitters transform the swap into parity of the relative modes. Equal independent displacement noise is invariant under that transformation. In the resulting frame,
\[
M
=
I_+\otimes
\frac1{(1+2x)^n}
\left(\frac{2x-1}{2x+1}\right)^{N_{-,\mathrm{total}}},
\qquad
F=(-1)^{N_{-,\mathrm{total}}}.
\]

Writing \(P_-=(I-F)/2\),
\[
P_E-P_B=-2\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho\otimes\rho)MP_-].
\]
The odd-sector eigenvalues have a definite sign on either side of \(1/2\), while
\[
\operatorname{Tr}[(\rho\otimes\rho)P_-]
=
\frac{1-\operatorname{Tr}\rho^2}{2}>0
\]
precisely for mixed inputs. Injectivity on the odd sector proves strictness even at infinite rank; no uniform spectral gap is assumed.

The complete proof is in [EXACT_PURITY_BOUNDARY.txt](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_f3da00dcc3948191a6918899ada18fa0&account_id=personal).

### Why this does not prove \(x_*=1/2\)

For a thermal input with mean photons \(s\),
\[
P_B=\frac1{2s+2x+1},
\qquad
P_E=\frac1{4xs+2x+1}.
\]
Its Rényi-2 entropy difference therefore tends to
\[
S_2(B)-S_2(E)\longrightarrow-\log_2(2x),
\]
which is positive for every \(x<1/2\).

But its von Neumann coherent information tends to
\[
I_c(\tau_s,\mathcal N_x)\longrightarrow-\log_2(ex),
\]
which is negative for \(x>1/e\).
